_meta.what: Governance-fragmentation dossier for Greater Mumbai — every body that took a function from the elected municipal corporation (MCGM/BMC), pre and post 1991. For each: WHAT (body + function taken), HOW (enabling instrument: Act name/year/number, notification, concession; decided_by = city|state|centre|colonial), WHY (stated rationale AND real political economy), ERA (pre_1991 developmental-state wave vs post_1991 neoliberal wave). The analytical core is decided_by: in almost every case the carve-out was authored by the STATE or CENTRE, never by the elected city.
_meta.thesis: Mumbai keeps the strongest in-house estate in the atlas (water, sewerage, BEST transport, major hospitals, fire — all in-house under the 1888 Act). Yet the high-rent functions — metropolitan land and planning, housing, slum land, the metro and its real estate, the port, the suburban grid — were lifted OUT of the elected corporation into state boards, SPVs and private concessions. This is Ghosh's improvement-regime (depoliticise development by handing it to an appointed, executive board) running from the 1898 Bombay Improvement Trust to the 2024 Dharavi SPV. The instrument changes — colonial trust, developmental-state authority, neoliberal SPV/PPP — but the decider does not: the elected city is the one body that almost never decides.

decided_by_legend.colonial: Pre-independence colonial state (Bombay Presidency / Government of Bombay).
decided_by_legend.state: Government of Maharashtra / State Legislature (the dominant decider here).
decided_by_legend.city: The elected Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM/BMC). Note how rarely this appears.

era_legend.pre_1991: Developmental-state wave: planning authorities, housing boards, new-town corporations built by the state to direct land and growth (CIDCO 1970, MMRDA 1975, MHADA 1976). The logic is dirigiste land assembly and depoliticised 'orderly development'.
era_legend.post_1991: Neoliberal wave: slum-as-real-estate (SRA 1995, cross-subsidy/TDR finance), single-purpose SPVs off the municipal books (MMRC, Maha Metro, Smart City), and private/PPP concessions (Adani electricity, Dharavi). The logic is land financialisation, off-balance-sheet delivery and private capital.

_meta.status: Authored 2026-06 from the loaded laws manifests (data/laws/mumbai/manifest.md verifies MMC Act 1888 = Bombay Act III of 1888 and MMRDA Act = Mah. NO fabrication.
sources_framing: Anwesha Ghosh, 'The Improvement Regime: Public Trusts, Real Estates, and India's Urban Futurities', Comparative Studies in Society and History (2025) [Zotero V295ZMA6] — the depoliticisation/recoupment frame.
Legg et al., 'Post-Colonial Developmentalities: From the Delhi Improvement Trust to the Delhi Development Authority' (2006) [Zotero 6TY79KRW] — trust->authority continuity.
Melinda Cooper, Counterrevolution (2024) — privatisation/SPV as counterrevolution against democratic claims on the economy; austerity-extravagance.

corporation.name: Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM / Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation, BMC)
corporation.act: The Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888 (Bombay Act III of 1888; orig. 'Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, 1888', renamed 'Mumbai' by Maharashtra Act XXV of 1996)
retains: Water supply (production + distribution, in-house — among the deepest municipal water operations in India)
Solid-waste management (in-house dept, though front line heavily contractualised — see contractualisation)
Public health — runs major municipal hospitals (KEM, Sion/LTMG, Nair) plus peripheral hospitals and dispensaries: unusually deep in-house municipal health
Urban transport + island-city electricity supply via the BEST Undertaking (a statutory undertaking of BMC under the 1888 Act — see parastatals note 'BEST')
Statutory planning authority for Greater Mumbai (but the powers flow from the MRTP Act 1966, a STATE statute, not the 1888 Act)
corporation.note: The 1888 Act gives BMC the strongest, most capacious in-house estate in the atlas (Mumbai scores ~83% on the devolution scorecard). The fragmentation below is therefore not total hollowing — it is the selective removal of the LAND-, FINANCE- and MEGAPROJECT-rich functions, leaving the labour-intensive service estate inside the elected body.

parastatals.name: Bombay City Improvement Trust (BIT)
parastatals.function_taken: Urban planning, land acquisition, slum/street clearance and infrastructure development — lifted out of the elected corporation into an appointed, executive board after the 1896 plague.

how.act: City of Bombay Improvement Act, 1898 (Bombay Act IV of 1898)

why.stated: Sanitary reconstruction of a plague-stricken city: open out congested districts, build arterial roads, reclaim land, rehouse the displaced — 'improvement' as technical-hygienic necessity.
why.real: The prototype of Ghosh's improvement regime: development lifted out of 'the stranglehold of municipal politics' into an executive board of appointed technocrats with the elected corporation reduced to a minority of seats. Rehousing the poor was the founding justification but became 'an idle afterthought'; the Trust financed itself by acquiring, redeveloping and SELLING surplus land at recoupment value — the city's first land-rentier machine. Depoliticisation + land financialisation, a century before the SPV.

parastatals.source: corporation_history.json (BIT 1898, post-1896 plague); docs/the-corporate-city.md; Kidambi, The Making of an Indian Metropolis (2007). Act number (Bombay Act IV of 1898) flagged for gazette confirmation.

parastatals.name: City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Ltd (CIDCO)
parastatals.function_taken: Urban planning, land assembly and new-town development for Navi Mumbai — a wholly new planned city built across the harbour to decongest Greater Mumbai, removing that growth (and its land value) entirely from BMC's jurisdiction.

how.act: Incorporated 17 March 1970 as a govt company under the Companies Act, 1956; designated New Town Development Authority for Navi Mumbai by State notification under the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 (Mah. XXXVII of 1966), s.113

why.stated: Decongest the island city by building a counter-magnet twin city; deliver 'orderly, planned' development of the mainland across Thane creek.
why.real: Developmental-state land machine: CIDCO compulsorily acquired ~private/village land at agricultural prices and monetised it as a planned-city landlord — the single largest public land-financialisation engine in the region, its surplus funding its own expansion (the recoupment logic at metropolitan scale). Growth was directed by an appointed corporation, not any elected city. Caste/labour offloading: original Agri/Koli villagers (the 'project-affected persons') were displaced into a decades-long, partly-unkept '12.5% scheme' rehabilitation.

parastatals.source: CIDCO 'About Us' / incorporation record (17 Mar 1970); MRTP Act 1966 s.113 (New Town Development Authority); service_providers.json (NMIAL: CIDCO 26%).

parastatals.name: Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA)
parastatals.function_taken: Planning for economic and social development AND large-scale urban/regional infrastructure at the metropolitan scale — the Regional Plan for the MMR, trunk infrastructure, major roads/flyovers, and several metro lines. The metropolitan-tier planning and megaproject function that a single empowered city government would otherwise hold.

how.act: Mumbai (orig. Bombay) Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act, 1974 (Maharashtra Act IV of 1975; assent published 18 Jan 1975)

why.stated: Plan, coordinate and supervise the 'orderly development' of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region across many municipal bodies; execute regional plans and metropolitan infrastructure beyond any single corporation's boundary.
why.real: The improvement trust reborn as the metropolitan development authority — an appointed, state-controlled body holding the region's land and megaproject pipeline above and outside the elected corporations. MMRDA self-finances heavily off land (BKC — the Bandra-Kurla Complex — is a state-owned commercial-land bank it leases/auctions at premium), making it a metropolitan rentier directly in Ghosh's 'recoupment' lineage. The Art. 243ZE Metropolitan Planning Committee (the CONSTITUTIONALLY mandated, part-elected integrator) is effectively displaced by MMRDA's executive planning role — a documented accountability gap. Decided wholly by the state.

parastatals.source: data/laws/mumbai/manifest.md (MMRDA Act = Mah. IV of 1975, verified); service_providers.json (MMRDA dominant planning/infra body); manifest note on MPC gap.

parastatals.name: Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA)
parastatals.function_taken: Public housing, area development, and — critically — the repair and redevelopment of Mumbai's old cessed buildings and the disposal of vast tracts of state housing land. Slum improvement / housing for weaker sections (12th-Schedule items 9, 10, 11) carved into a state board rather than the elected corporation.

how.act: Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Act, 1976 (commonly cited 1976; enacted/published as Maharashtra Act XXVIII of 1977) — consolidated the former Bombay Housing Board, Maharashtra Housing Board, Vidarbha Housing Board, Bombay Building Repairs & Reconstruction Board and Slum Improvement Board into one authority

why.stated: Unify fragmented housing boards into a single authority to provide affordable housing, repair dangerous cessed buildings (funded by a repair cess on tenants), and undertake area development.
why.real: Consolidation gave the STATE a single, appointed custodian of Mumbai's most valuable redevelopment asset class — old cessed buildings on prime island-city land and large MHADA land banks. Redevelopment via TDR and incentive-FSI turned a welfare-housing mandate into a land-financialisation lever captured by builders; the elected corporation, which permits the construction, does not control the land or the scheme. Housing-as-real-estate, decided by the state board, not the city.

parastatals.source: MHADA Act 1976/1977; corporation_history.json lineage of housing boards. Exact gazette act-number (Mah. XXVIII of 1977) flagged for confirmation.

parastatals.name: Slum Rehabilitation Authority (SRA)
parastatals.function_taken: Slum improvement, clearance and redevelopment for Greater Mumbai (12th-Schedule item 10) — the single most valuable land-development function in the city, since ~40% of Mumbaikars live in slums on land that redevelopment converts to saleable FSI. Taken from both the corporation and the general slum machinery and vested in a dedicated appointed authority.

how.act: Constituted under the Maharashtra Slum Areas (Improvement, Clearance and Redevelopment) Act, 1971 as amended in 1995 (insertion of Chapter I-A / the Slum Rehabilitation Authority provisions) operating with the MRTP Act 1966; SRA notified as the Planning Authority for slum areas in Greater Mumbai, 1995

why.stated: Provide free in-situ rehabilitation housing to eligible slum-dwellers at no cost to the public exchequer, by letting developers cross-subsidise rehab tenements with free-sale flats and TDR — the 'Mumbai model' of market-financed slum housing (origin in the 1995 Shiv Sena-BJP government's promise of free housing to 40 lakh slum-dwellers).
why.real: The purest land-financialisation instrument in the atlas: slum land is reclassified as a development resource, the slum-dweller becomes a planning input, and the rent flows to developers via free-sale FSI and TDR. The elected corporation is bypassed (SRA is the planning authority for slums, appointed and state-controlled); the appointed board is a site of intense builder/elite capture and patronage. Depoliticisation (slums as a technical redevelopment problem) + land financialisation (Ghosh's recoupment) + offloading the housing of the labouring/Dalit-Muslim poor onto a developer-driven scheme that routinely under-delivers and under-houses.

parastatals.source: Maharashtra Slum Areas Act 1971 (1995 amendment constituting SRA); MRTP Act 1966; widely documented 'Mumbai model'. Exact 1995 amending-act number flagged for gazette confirmation.

parastatals.name: Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (MMRC / MMRCL)
parastatals.function_taken: Mass urban transit — construction and operation of Metro Line 3 (the underground Colaba-Bandra-SEEPZ line). Public transport (12th-Schedule item 17 territory) delivered through an off-the-municipal-books special-purpose vehicle rather than through BMC/BEST.

how.act: Incorporated 2014 as a 50:50 special-purpose joint-venture company of the Government of India and Government of Maharashtra under the Companies Act, 2013, operating under the (central) Metro Railways (Operation & Maintenance) Act, 2002 framework

why.stated: Deliver high-capacity rapid transit quickly with ring-fenced finance (JICA/loan-funded) and dedicated project management, beyond the capacity/remit of the municipal transport undertaking.
why.real: The SPV is Cooper's counterrevolution in institutional form: a single-purpose, off-balance-sheet company that ring-fences a megaproject's land, debt and revenue from democratic budgeting and from the elected city. BEST — the BMC's own transit undertaking that actually moves the daily commuter — is starved while capital and prime depot/station real estate flow to the metro SPV (note the Aarey car-shed land conflict). Decided by state+centre as joint shareholders; the elected city is not a controlling party. Austerity for the bus, extravagance for the metro.

parastatals.source: MMRC incorporation 2014, 50:50 GoI-GoM SPV; service_providers.json (Line 3 by MMRC). Metro Railways O&M Act 2002 applicability flagged.

parastatals.name: Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (Maha Metro) + MMRDA metro lines
parastatals.function_taken: Construction/operation of further Mumbai-region metro lines (and elsewhere in Maharashtra) — additional mass-transit corridors delivered by MMRDA and the state SPV rather than the elected city.

how.act: Maha Metro incorporated 2016 as a 50:50 GoI-GoM SPV under the Companies Act, 2013; several Mumbai-region metro lines executed directly by MMRDA under the MMRDA Act 1974

why.stated: A standing state-level metro implementing agency to roll out multiple corridors with shared expertise and central co-funding.
why.real: Same SPV logic as MMRC, generalised: transit and its station/depot real estate held by state-controlled vehicles, the elected corporation a bystander. MMRDA's direct execution of lines folds the metro into its existing land-rentier model (transit raises land value MMRDA then captures).

parastatals.source: Maha Metro incorporation 2016 (50:50 SPV); service_providers.json (other lines by MMRDA). Line-by-line split flagged.

parastatals.name: Dharavi Redevelopment Project SPV (Navbharat Mega Developers Pvt Ltd)
parastatals.function_taken: Redevelopment of Dharavi — slum redevelopment (12th-Schedule item 10) of one of Asia's largest informal settlements on ~240+ hectares of prime central-city land — handed to a state-private SPV, removing the function from both the corporation and the ordinary SRA route via a bespoke project authority.

how.act: Dharavi Redevelopment Project / Slum Rehabilitation Authority special-project framework; global tender re-floated 2022, won by Adani (Adani Properties/Adani Realty) 2022-2023; project SPV 'Navbharat Mega Developers Pvt Ltd' incorporated with Adani majority (~80%) and Government of Maharashtra (~20%), 2023-2024

why.stated: Finally redevelop Dharavi after decades of failed attempts, delivering rehab housing and modern infrastructure through a single capable developer with deep capital.
why.real: The terminus of the whole lineage: the city's most valuable slum land, converted into a developer-led real-estate play through a bespoke SPV in which a single private conglomerate holds the controlling stake and the state holds a minority — elite capture written into the cap table. Contested grants of additional land (salt-pan, railway land), TDR generated for use across the city, and eligibility cut-offs that exclude large numbers of residents make this land financialisation + labour/caste offloading at its sharpest. The elected corporation decides almost nothing; the state authored the concession.

parastatals.source: privatization_map.json (_adani_concentration); DRP/SRA special-project record; widely reported Adani-GoM SPV (Navbharat Mega Developers, ~80:20). Exact stake/incorporation date flagged.

parastatals.name: Mumbai Smart City / area-based SPVs (Smart Cities Mission)
parastatals.function_taken: Area-based municipal development and service delivery within designated 'smart city' zones — planning, infrastructure and some service functions routed through a corporate SPV with a state-appointed CEO, partially displacing the elected corporation's authority over its own area.

how.act: Smart Cities Mission (Government of India, 2015) special-purpose-vehicle model — SPV incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, board chaired/run by appointed officials, central+state funding

why.stated: Fast, ring-fenced, professionally-managed delivery of 'smart' area infrastructure with dedicated central funds.
why.real: The Mission mandated an SPV with executive (not elected) control of Mission funds and projects in every city — a structural transfer of authority from the elected council to a corporate vehicle, decided by the centre and run by appointees. Even where the corporation holds equity it does not control the board: depoliticisation by corporate form, the improvement-trust template digitised.

parastatals.source: Smart Cities Mission SPV model (MoHUA, 2015). Mumbai-specific SPV scope/status flagged for confirmation.

parastatals.name: Mumbai Port Authority (formerly Mumbai Port Trust, MbPT)
parastatals.function_taken: The port and its vast central-city land estate (~750+ ha along the eastern waterfront) — never the corporation's, but a major slice of the city's land and frontage held by a CENTRAL body entirely outside both the elected city and the state.

how.act: Originally under the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 (central); reconstituted as the Mumbai Port Authority under the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021 (central Act 15 of 2021)

why.stated: National-interest management of a major port as central infrastructure.
why.real: Included as the limit case of the unelected city: a central authority sits on a huge tract of prime eastern-seafront land whose redevelopment (the 'Port Lands' / eastern-waterfront opening) is one of Mumbai's largest land questions — decided by the centre, with the elected city having no controlling say. The land-rentier logic, but at the central tier.

parastatals.source: Major Port Trusts Act 1963; Major Port Authorities Act 2021 (Act 15 of 2021).

parastatals.name: BEST Undertaking (Brihanmumbai Electric Supply & Transport) — COUNTER-EXAMPLE
parastatals.function_taken: NONE taken from the city — included as the deliberate counter-example. BEST runs the island-city BUS transport and the island-city ELECTRICITY supply, and it IS the elected corporation's own statutory undertaking.

how.act: Constituted as a statutory undertaking/committee of BMC under the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888 (Bombay Act III of 1888)

why.stated: Municipal provision of transport and power to citizens as a public undertaking of the elected corporation.
why.real: BEST proves the point by inversion: where a function stays INSIDE the elected body it is delivered as a municipal undertaking answerable (however imperfectly) to councillors — and it is precisely this in-house transit that has been starved as capital flows to the off-the-books metro SPVs. The contrast between BEST (city-decided, declining) and MMRC/Maha Metro (state-decided, capital-rich) is the fragmentation thesis in a single city.

parastatals.source: data/laws/mumbai/manifest.md (BEST is a BMC undertaking under the 1888 Act); service_providers.json; Zotero TCU63NAH (collapsing bus ridership).

contractualisation.name: Sanitation / conservancy contract labour (safai kamgar)
contractualisation.function_hollowed: Public health, sanitation, conservancy and SWM (12th-Schedule item 6) — nominally in-house under BMC, but the front-line workforce is split into a permanent tier and a precarious contract tier doing identical work.

how.instrument: labour contracting / outsourcing within the BMC SWM department
how.note: Unlike the parastatal carve-outs (state/centre-decided), this hollowing is decided WITHIN the corporation's own administration — the elected body contractualising its own front line.

contractualisation.detail: ~28,000 PERMANENT + ~6,500-7,000 CONTRACT safai kamgar, PLUS ~9,000 'dattak vasti' (slum) workers via community orgs who are not even counted as contract workers. Contract workers do identical duties under the same municipal officers but earn ~Rs 14,500/mo vs ~Rs 24,000 permanent; dattak-vasti workers are wholly off the books. Genuinely-precarious share ~30-35% of the front line.
contractualisation.why_real: Ghosh's corporate municipality + Cooper's privatisation-as-counterrevolution landing on Ambedkar's terrain: the contracted front line is overwhelmingly Dalit/Valmiki (NAMASTE profiling: ~69% SC, ~77% Dalit, ~92% SC/ST/OBC). Contractualisation is a caste-justice machine — 'division of labour is also a division of labourers' — splitting one job into a secure mixed-caste tier and a precarious Dalit tier. Regularisation came only by litigation (SC 2017 ordered permanency for 2,700; SC 2025 directed BMC to retain 580), never as policy. Sewer/septic deaths fall on this contract/informal layer.
contractualisation.source: contractualization_map.json (mumbai.sanitation_conservancy); Scroll 'Jailed for keeping Mumbai clean'; IndiaSpend/Business Standard (wage gap); NewsClick (580 workers, 2025 SC order); NAMASTE caste profiling.

contractualisation.name: Solid-waste transport / collection concessions
contractualisation.function_hollowed: Solid-waste collection and transport (12th-Schedule item 6) — BMC retains the dumping ground and core department but contracts out a share of transport/collection.

how.instrument: O&M / transport concession to private operators
how.note: BMC-let contracts (e.g. Antony Waste Handling and others operate in the Mumbai region) alongside its own fleet.

contractualisation.detail: Transport/collection partly contracted; BMC retains dumping-ground and core dept. Operator mix not fully enumerated.
contractualisation.why_real: The 'in-house'/GREEN sanitation cell on the scorecard is the most hollow cell across the atlas — even Mumbai's relatively strong corporation routes part of the lift through private concessions, the OPERATION privatised beneath a public org chart.

private_carveouts.name: Adani Electricity Mumbai Ltd (AEML) + Tata Power — suburban distribution
private_carveouts.function: Electricity distribution to suburban Mumbai (NB: NOT a 12th-Schedule municipal function — included for the unelected-city/democratic-deficit point, not as a devolution failure).

how.instrument: private acquisition under the Electricity Act, 2003
how.note: Adani acquired Reliance Infrastructure's Mumbai power business (~Rs 18,800 cr) in 2018; private lineage via BSES/Reliance from the 20th century. Tata Power holds a parallel licence.

private_carveouts.why_real: Cooper's frame: ~12M+ suburban Mumbaikars depend daily on a private monopoly they cannot vote out, regulated only by MERC. The elected corporation runs water/roads/waste; the suburban grid answers to shareholders. (Island-city power stays with BEST, the BMC undertaking — see counter-example.)

private_carveouts.name: Mumbai airports — CSMIA + Navi Mumbai (Adani)
private_carveouts.function: Airport operation (critical public infrastructure; not a municipal function) — both of Mumbai's commercial airports under one private group.

how.note: Adani took over CSMIA from GVK (2021); Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIAL — MIAL ~74%, CIDCO 26%) opened Dec 2025.

private_carveouts.why_real: Concentration of the city's entire air gateway in one unelected conglomerate — the 'unelected city' at its most concentrated (see privatization_map _adani_concentration).

timeline_note: Two waves, one decider. PRE-1991 (developmental state): Bombay Improvement Trust 1898 (colonial prototype) -> CIDCO 1970 (new-town land machine) -> MMRDA 1975 (metropolitan land/planning authority) -> MHADA 1976 (consolidated housing/cessed-land board). All state/colonial-decided; all built to direct LAND and growth through appointed boards. POST-1991 (neoliberal): SRA 1995 (slum-as-real-estate) -> Mumbai Smart City SPV 2015 -> MMRC 2014 / Maha Metro 2016 (transit SPVs) -> Adani suburban electricity 2018 -> CSMIA 2021 / NMIA 2025 -> Dharavi SPV 2023 (slum land to a private-majority SPV). The pre-1991 wave used state AUTHORITIES; the post-1991 wave uses SPVs and PPPs — off-balance-sheet, single-purpose, increasingly private-majority. ACROSS BOTH WAVES the decider is the STATE or CENTRE, essentially never the elected city: of the ~12 carve-outs here, the city decided ZERO of the major land/transit/housing transfers (the only 'city'-decided items are BEST staying in-house and the corporation contractualising its own sanitation labour). That is the dossier's headline: Mumbai keeps the broadest in-house service estate in the atlas, yet every rent-rich function — land, slums, housing, metro, port, suburban grid — was lifted out of the one body Mumbaikars elect, by governments they did not.
